To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the formation and retention of platelet aggregates and leukocytes in the coronary circulation is an important determinant of postischemic dysfunction of the heart and (2) the formation and release of platelet aggregates in the coronary circulation are determined by the balance between the platelet activating and inhibiting factors.

(1) intravascular microaggregation of platelets and leukocytes contributes to postischemia myocardial dysfunction, (2) this process is initiated and sustained by the formation of microaggregates, (3) microaggregates are retained in the microcirculation by the formation of platelet-leukocyte aggregates, and (4) the process can be inhibited by the administration of a platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor.
intravascular microaggregate retention in coronary microvessels contributes to the development of myocardial dysfunction after coronary occlusion and reperfusion.
